title: Transactional commit orchestrator for batching/caching recommendations with idempotent API
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Goal: Implement a resilient, SDK-friendly transactional commit orchestration layer for Optimize recommendations that supports safe apply, deterministic rollback, and webhook-driven automation with strong idempotency guarantees.

Background: Optimize generates batching and KV-caching recommendations that may be applied automatically or via operator confirmation. Production usage requires: (1) exactly-once semantics for applies where possible, (2) clear rollback semantics when a plan is rejected or causes regressions, (3) webhook hooks for external orchestration, and (4) SDK primitives to make retries and deduplication safe for customers and the console.

Scope: backend API surface + lightweight orchestration hooks + SDK ergonomics. Not in scope: UI console changes (tracked separately) and on-prem agent packaging.

Design decisions and constraints:
- Commit model: three-phase flow: propose -> commit -> finalize. Propose creates an immutable proposal object (id + spec + pre-apply diff + heuristics). Commit is idempotent and returns a commit token and final diff. Finalize acknowledges completion. This minimizes race conditions between autoscale/optimizer and operators.
- Idempotency: primary dedup key model will be: idempotency_key = sha256(customer_id + proposal_id + client_nonce). Servers will store idempotency records for 72 hours by default. SDK will surface a createCommit() helper that auto-generates client_nonce and retries safely.
- Fencing: to avoid split-brain when multiple scheduler instances or retries hit the system, commits are guarded by a monotonically increasing proposal_revision (integer). Commit attempts that provide an older revision will be rejected with HTTP 409 and a suggested reconcile token.
- Exactly-once vs at-least-once: true exactly-once across distributed systems is expensive. We aim for strongly idempotent at-least-once with compensating rollback and an eventual reconciliation pass that ensures system convergence.
- Webhooks: webhook semantics include delivery handshake, ack protocol, and a replay-safe event id. Webhook payloads include proposal_id, commit_token (if present), and a short patch summary. Consumers are expected to persist event_id to deduplicate. We will support configurable retry/backoff and a DLQ for failing webhook deliveries.
- Observability: emit metrics: optimize.proposals.created, optimize.commits.succeeded, optimize.commits.rejected, optimize.rollbacks.triggered, optimize.commit.latency, optimize.webhook.failures. Traces will be included via the existing tracing hook with span tags for customer_id, proposal_id, and commit_token.

Proposed HTTP surface (for discussion):
- POST /optimize/v1/proposals  (create proposal)
  body: {customer_id, spec, reason, preview_window_days}
  returns 201 + {proposal_id, preview_summary, proposal_revision}

- POST /optimize/v1/proposals/:id/commit  (idempotent apply)
  headers: Idempotency-Key (optional), X-Client-Nonce (optional)
  body: {requested_revision, apply_options: {dry_run:false, force:false}}
  returns 200 + {commit_token, effective_revision, actions_applied, conflicts: []} or 409

- POST /optimize/v1/commits/:token/finalize  (ack finalize)
  body: {ack_details}
  returns 200

- POST /optimize/v1/commits/:token/rollback  (trigger rollback)
  body: {reason, initiated_by}
  returns 200 + {rollback_id}

- Webhook endpoint: configurable per-customer with event types: proposal.created, commit.succeeded, commit.failed, rollback.started. Each webhook includes event_id, timestamp, and replayable payload.

SDK ergonomics (JS/Go):
- createProposal(spec) -> returns Proposal object with .commit() helper that accepts idempotencyKey and retryOptions.
- commitWithRetries(proposalId, opts) -> handles 409s by fetching latest revision and returning either success or a reconcile-needed error.
- onWebhookEvent(event) -> SDK helper to validate signature, dedupe via event_id, and surface typed events to application code.

Security & review notes:
- Commit tokens are bearer-coded but short-lived (TTL default 5m). They must not contain privileged scope; finalization/rollback endpoints will additionally validate the caller's org.
- Audit logs required for any commit/rollback action (who/when/what). Ensure integration with existing KMS audit pipeline.

Trade-offs considered:
- Keeping idempotency state for 72h increases storage but reduces accidental double-applies. We considered a shorter TTL (24h) but that increases the chance of duplicate work for long-running retries from flaky clients.
- Using proposal_revision for fencing requires optimistic updates in some places; alternative was a leader-election lock but that added cross-region complexity.

Acceptance criteria:
- API endpoints implemented and covered by contract tests for idempotency/replay and revision fences.
- SDK helpers implemented for JS and Go with integration tests against a test harness that simulates retries and webhook replays.
- Console/workflow teams can toggle auto-apply per-customer; a rollout will begin to 10% of customers in staging before gradual ramp.
- Metrics and traces emitted; dashboards created in Grafana with alert for spike in commit.rejected > 1% of commits.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged internal canary for internal teams (1 week)
2) Staging test with 10 customers (2 weeks)
3) Gradual ramp to 50% with monitoring gates (2 weeks)
4) Full rollout after OKRs/metrics stable (ongoing)
